summary: Backend-only test for the new Sadaqah/Stripe monetization feature plus regression on existing endpoints. Pytest run against external REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL: 18 of 19 tests passed. New Sadaqah checkout creation works perfectly for all 4 packages (small=$3, medium=$7, large=$20, custom=$15.50) — each returns a real cs_test_... session_id and a https://checkout.stripe.com/c/pay/... URL. Server-side price-tampering protection works: custom_amount<$1, custom_amount>$1000, unknown package, and missing custom_amount with package=custom all return 400. MongoDB payment_transactions row is correctly inserted with status='initiated', payment_status='pending', amount, package, currency='usd' and metadata at the moment the session is created (verified directly against MongoDB). Regression: /api/chat (Claude Sonnet 4.5 via Emergent), /api/group/create + /join + /checkin + /get, /api/gates and /api/gates/nearest, /api/progress upsert/get all still pass. ONE backend bug found: GET /api/sadaqah/status/{session_id} returns 500 for sessions that were just successfully created — the Emergent Stripe proxy raises 'No such checkout.session' on stripe.checkout.Session.retrieve. Reproduced consistently with delays of 0s/2s/5s/10s after creation; not eventual consistency. Frontend SadaqahSuccess.jsx polling will fail because of this. The /api/webhook/stripe endpoint was intentionally not exercised per the request notes.

critical.issue: Returns 500 Internal Server Error for sessions that were JUST successfully created by POST /api/sadaqah/checkout. Stripe (via the Emergent integrations proxy at https://integrations.emergentagent.com/stripe) responds with 'No such checkout.session: cs_test_...' on stripe.checkout.Session.retrieve, even though the same proxy created the session and returned a valid checkout URL. This breaks the SadaqahSuccess polling flow — after a real donor pays, the frontend will keep polling and getting 500s. Reproduced 4 times in a row over 0/2/5/10s delays. Root cause is most likely on the Emergent Stripe proxy side (the test-mode proxy may not implement Session.retrieve, or sessions are not persisted on its side), but the route ALSO has no error handling — emergentintegrations.payments.stripe.checkout.CheckoutError bubbles up as a bare 500. Two-part fix recommended: (1) wrap the get_checkout_status call in try/except and return a structured JSON ({status:'unknown', payment_status:'pending'}) plus 200 so the frontend can keep polling without breaking, OR return 404 with a clear detail; (2) confirm with Emergent integrations team whether Session.retrieve is supported on sk_test_emergent. As an interim mitigation, the polling endpoint can also fall back to reading payment_transactions from MongoDB and (for sessions still in 'initiated') return {status:'open', payment_status:'pending'} until the webhook flips it to paid.

minor.issue: amount=0 or amount<0 path is partially blocked: if package==custom + custom_amount<=0, our code returns 400 (good), but emergentintegrations also enforces amount>0 inside CheckoutSessionRequest validator. The two layers should be consolidated; current code is fine but redundant validation on amount<=0 is split across files.

Pydantic SadaqahCheckoutRequest accepts custom_amount as float without bounds-clamping at the model level (only inside the route). If someone reuses this model elsewhere later, the amount-cap can be missed. Consider Field(ge=1, le=1000) on custom_amount.

Not tested per request brief, but a quick code-read shows the route uses request.headers.get('Stripe-Signature', '') — Stripe sends the header lowercase 'stripe-signature' which Starlette is case-insensitive about (this is fine), but the StripeCheckout.handle_webhook signature-verification path needs webhook_secret to be set on the StripeCheckout instance — currently _stripe_for() does NOT pass webhook_secret, so any inbound webhook signature verification is effectively a no-op or will fail. Set STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET in env and pass it to StripeCheckout(api_key=..., webhook_secret=..., webhook_url=...) before going to production.

integration_issues.issue: Once the user lands on /sadaqah/success?session_id=cs_test_..., the page polls /api/sadaqah/status/{session_id} which currently 500s. So even after a successful Stripe payment, the success page will not show the 'paid' confirmation. This is caused by the backend issue above, not by the frontend code.

action_items: Fix /api/sadaqah/status/{session_id} so it does not return a bare 500 when Stripe.retrieve fails. Wrap the call in try/except CheckoutError; on error, fall back to reading payment_transactions from MongoDB and return {status:'open', payment_status:'pending'} (or whatever was last persisted by the webhook) with HTTP 200, so the frontend SadaqahSuccess polling does not break.

Investigate why the Emergent Stripe proxy says 'No such checkout.session' for sessions it just minted (sk_test_emergent + https://integrations.emergentagent.com/stripe). Either the proxy doesn't support Session.retrieve, or the session is created on a different Stripe account than the one used for retrieve. Without this working end-to-end, paid status will only flip via webhook, so make sure the webhook route is signature-verified and idempotent.
Set STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET in /app/backend/.env and pass it through _stripe_for() so /api/webhook/stripe can verify Stripe-Signature header.
Add Pydantic-level bounds (ge=1, le=1000) on SadaqahCheckoutRequest.custom_amount as defense-in-depth alongside the route-level check.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py /api/sadaqah/status has no try/except — any error from the Stripe integration becomes a 500 with no structure; the polling frontend cannot distinguish 'not found' from 'server down' from 'still pending'.

server.py /api/webhook/stripe constructs StripeCheckout without webhook_secret, so signature verification in handle_webhook is unreliable. Move STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET out of env and into _stripe_for().
server.py SADAQAH_PACKAGES is hardcoded — fine for v1, but as soon as you add a 4th preset or run a Ramadan campaign, it should move to a config collection or env JSON to avoid redeploys.
server.py file is ~470 lines and growing; consider splitting routers: routes/chat.py, routes/group.py, routes/sadaqah.py once it crosses 600 lines.

The payment_transactions row writes both 'status' and 'payment_status' — webhook handler sets status='complete' when payment_status=='paid', but for refund/expired flows there is no path. Add an explicit mapping (status from Stripe event_type) so the DB can show 'expired'/'refunded' too.

_stripe_for() recomputes webhook_url from request.base_url — in K8s behind a proxy this can sometimes be http:// internal — explicitly use REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL or a new BACKEND_PUBLIC_URL env var so the webhook URL Stripe sees is always correct.

Pydantic SadaqahCheckoutRequest.origin_url is required but not URL-validated; pass it through HttpUrl for safety, otherwise an attacker can craft a phishing redirect via the success_url (Stripe will reject obvious mismatches but defense-in-depth is cheap).

success_rate.backend: 94.7% (18/19 pytest tests pass; 1 hard failure on /api/sadaqah/status due to Stripe proxy retrieve)

test_credentials: STRIPE_API_KEY=sk_test_emergent (already in /app/backend/.env), EMERGENT_LLM_KEY (already set). No user creds required.
seed_data_creation: Created ~6 payment_transactions rows in MongoDB during the run (one per checkout test) — all have status='initiated', payment_status='pending'. Safe to leave; or clean with: db.payment_transactions.deleteMany({metadata.source:'sunnah_umrah_app', payment_status:'pending'}).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: pytest /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py -v --tb=short --junitxml=/app/test_reports/pytest/pytest_results.xml. The single failing test is test_sadaqah_status — it depends on Stripe Session.retrieve working through the Emergent proxy. Once main agent fixes the route to fall back on the MongoDB payment_transactions row when Stripe retrieve fails, that test will need to be updated to expect a 200 with {status, payment_status} fields. The Stripe Checkout URL pattern confirmed working: https://checkout.stripe.com/c/pay/cs_test_a1HjEXUZkr4N... All 4 packages (small/medium/large/custom) successfully create sessions. Tampering protection (custom<$1, custom>$1000, unknown package, missing custom_amount) all return 400 as required. MongoDB payment_transactions persistence verified via direct motor query inside the test.
rca_of_the_issue: /api/sadaqah/status returns 500. Reproduction: 1) POST /api/sadaqah/checkout {package:'small', origin_url:'https://...'} → 200 with {url:'https://checkout.stripe.com/c/pay/cs_test_...', session_id:'cs_test_...'}. 2) Immediately GET /api/sadaqah/status/{that session_id} → 500 'Internal Server Error'. Backend log: emergentintegrations.payments.stripe.checkout.CheckoutError: Failed to retrieve session status: Request req_xxx: No such checkout.session: cs_test_xxx. The error originates in stripe.checkout.Session.retrieve() inside the emergentintegrations library, going through stripe.api_base='https://integrations.emergentagent.com/stripe' (set when api_key contains 'sk_test_emergent'). Both create and retrieve hit the same proxy with the same key; create succeeds, retrieve says session doesn't exist. Root cause is on the Emergent Stripe proxy side — likely the proxy does not implement Session.retrieve in test mode, or stores sessions in a way retrieve cannot find them. Mitigation in our code: catch CheckoutError, fall back to MongoDB payment_transactions row, and return whatever was last set by the webhook (which is the source of truth for production anyway). Long-term: confirm with Emergent integrations support whether retrieve is supported, and if not, document that polling /api/sadaqah/status is webhook-driven only (not Stripe-driven).
